source.title: Les Houches lectures on deep learning at large and infinite width
source.authors: Yasaman Bahri; Boris Hanin; Antonin Brossollet; Vittorio Erba; Christian Keup; Rosalba Pacelli; James B. Simon

record.file_problem: The full lecture text is present; no material cutoff or garbling affects the relevant sections.
record.tranche_reason: The lectures derive training dynamics for a simplified one-hidden-layer linear network with squared loss, addressing the learning-rate behavior in V5 through a different model from its cited deep-network examples.
record.gate_note: The lectures describe empirical catapult observations in realistic deep networks as findings from cited work [17]; those are not this study's own results and are not rows. The rows below capture the lectures' own analysis of the simplified model.
record.test_reason: These lecture notes explain and rederive established results. Section 3 introduces catapult dynamics from [17], an original source for V5; Section 3.3 develops that account rather than reporting an independent test. The record incorrectly treats the tutorial derivations as new study results.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the qualitative catapult dynamics but misstates their provenance: the simplified-model analysis and realistic-network observations are part of a pedagogical account of prior work [17]. Equation (113) additionally describes reaching arbitrarily small loss near the critical learning rate. The lectures broadly explain infinite-width limits and finite-width corrections rather than present an independent catapult study.
record.recipe_differences: The lectures derive dynamics for a one-hidden-layer linear network with one sample and squared loss; realistic deep-network observations are cited from prior work rather than newly tested here.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning rate changes the outcome: below 2/λ₀ the toy model follows constant-NTK dynamics; between 2/λ₀ and 4/λ₀ it exhibits catapult dynamics; above 4/λ₀ it diverges.

fits_no_version.finding: The lectures derive initialization-time signal correlations, Jacobian moments and depth-to-width scaling of NTK fluctuations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Depth relative to width controls fluctuations and departures from infinite-width behavior in randomly initialized networks.

record.peer_reviewed: Journal of Statistical Mechanics: Theory and Experiment
record.problems: The direct training analysis is for a highly simplified one-sample linear model. The text gives no uncertainty estimates or controls for this analysis. Realistic-network observations are cited, not newly reported results.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Empirical observations on realistic deep networks in Section 3.3 are attributed to cited work [17], so they are excluded.

untested.parts: All components: convolutional classification training error, label corruption, capacity, stopping and regularization.
All components: ReLU teacher-student spurious minima and extra student neurons.
All components: comparative training error with depth, identity shortcuts and the specified alternative recipes.

Comparative learning speed and trainable depth under different initializations. Signal propagation and Jacobian statistics are derived, while actual trainability findings are attributed to prior literature.
No independent test. Catapult recovery and divergence are explained through prior theory; edge-of-stability hovering and below-threshold divergence are not tested.
All components: batch-normalization speed and learning-rate comparisons, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: Excluding cited empirical observations while counting the accompanying rederivation as independent evidence creates an attribution inconsistency. No verdict labels are warranted for this lecture account.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 training error, random or corrupted labels, network size, and stopping or regularization effects.
Teacher-student ReLU landscapes, spurious minima, and student width.
Depth effects on classification training error, residual shortcuts, and normalization.
Comparative initialization effects on training speed or trainable depth; initialization and signal-propagation theory are discussed, but no such training result is reported as the lectures' own.
Realistic wide/deep network experiments; stochastic training; sharpness hovering at the stability threshold over long training; and runs that diverge below the threshold.
Batch-normalization comparisons and Fixup training results.

rows.subject: single hidden-layer NN, f(x) = 1/√n vᵀux
rows.operation_detail: Analyzed gradient descent on squared loss for one sample (x, y) = (1, 0), with n0 = 1.
rows.measure: Training loss and function value dynamics
rows.value: The NTK stays constant (λt = λ₀); the function value and loss converge exponentially in time.
rows.note: The lectures' derived toy-model result for the below-threshold regime.
rows.check: A below-threshold control cannot establish above-threshold recovery. This is also a tutorial derivation of prior results, not an independent result row. Constant NTK holds in the infinite-width limit; at large finite width the text specifies O(1/n) corrections.

source_check.correct: Exact constant NTK and exponential convergence apply in the n → ∞ limit for 0 < η < 2/λ₀. At large finite width, the dynamics have O(1/n) corrections. This below-threshold control cannot establish above-threshold recovery.
source_check.locator_found: Section 3.3, p. 25, equations (110)–(111) and following paragraph.
source_check.problem: The condition omits the infinite-width limit required for exact constant NTK; this tutorial result also should not count as independent evidence.

rows.subject: single hidden-layer NN, f(x) = 1/√n vᵀux
rows.operation_detail: Analyzed gradient descent on squared loss for one sample (x, y) = (1, 0).
rows.measure: Training loss and function value dynamics
rows.baseline: Initial loss and curvature at initialization; exact baseline value not stated.
rows.value: The function and loss initially increase; curvature adjusts, and the function and loss converge to a finite value.
rows.note: The lectures call this the catapult regime and say the initial increase occurs as n becomes large.
rows.check: The behavior matches the catapult component of V5, but this rederivation of [17] should not be an independent result row. Low-loss recovery is supported by equation (113), which describes time to O(ε) loss on either side of the threshold; convergence to a finite value alone would be insufficient. The growth argument uses strict inequalities, so behavior exactly at the stated endpoints is not established by that argument.

source_check.problem: The reported dynamics match the text, but the lectures rederive prior catapult results attributed to [17]; this should not count as an independent result row.
